thread:
Kara (product): quick sync — we need to align SLA boundaries vs entitlement language for the upcoming pilot. customers asking for 99.9% uptime + softcap credits.
Devon (sales): +1. customer A wants explicit surge protection in contract, but can accept higher price for guaranteed throughput.
Maya (finance): we need a clear cost model for surge credits — otherwise margin hit. propose: burst credits as charged addon or prepaid bucket.
Ravi (legal): we can't promise hard credits without defining outage taxonomy. need definitions for 'service outage', 'degraded performance', and 'force majeure'.
Leo (solutions): from field: most customers want an escape hatch when dedicated capacity fails — automatic fallback to hosted variants, with rate-limited fallback. Customers also want priority lane during incidents.
Kara (product): options I see: (A) conservative: SLA 99.5% for starter tiers, 99.9% for enterprise with explicit credit formula; (B) bold: 99.9% across, with contractual burst pool and operational playbook. thoughts?
Devon (sales): Option B sells better but will create support escalations. we should gate B to committed annual spend > $X.
Maya (finance): agree — gate by commit. also require a non-refundable buffer to cover expected burst cost for first 3 months.
Ravi (legal): sketch of contract clause: "Credits calculated as % of monthly fee for verified outages where SLA not met; credits do not exceed X% and are subject to customer-provided telemetry and our incident verification." Need to add explicit excluded events.
Ava (pm): can we define operational playbook as part of the offering? e.g., canary fallbacks, priority routing, and escalation timelines (T+15m ack, T+1h mitigation plan). Make playbook an attachment so it's visible in sales cycle.
Leo (solutions): yes — add runbook excerpt. sample snippet to include in deck:
```
If dedicated pool fails, route to hosted pool with throttled qps and 30s reconnect guidance. Notify customer via webhook + slack channel.
```
Kara (product): decision proposal: pilot with two paths: enterprise pilot = Option B gated by 12mo commit + prepaid burst bucket; self-serve = Option A. Add quantified credit formula and runbook.
Devon (sales): fine. need pricing bullets for AE to negotiate: prepaid burst bucket sizes (10k/100k/1M token bundles) and per-token overage.
Maya (finance): I'll model margin impact by EOD tomorrow. need expected burst utilization % from ops.
ops-bot: new incident metric report ready: 30d median dedicated failover time = 42s, 95th = 6m. Link: https://internal.ops/reports/failover-30d
Leo (solutions): that failover curve supports Option B with throttled fallback — less risky than I thought.
Ravi (legal): I'll draft the contract addendum and exclusion list. will share redlines by Thu.
Kara (product): action items: Maya model margin + pricing tiers; Leo prepare runbook excerpt for deck; Ravi draft contract addendum; Devon prepare customer negotiation bullets. sync Fri 10am. :calendar: :white_check_mark:
Devon (sales): noted. I'll prep objections playbook.
Maya (finance): noted. will share model in sheet.
Ava (pm): I'll update the roadmap ticket with gating criteria and acceptance tests.
Kara (product): thanks team. keeping this in-thread for traceability.
